# Mobile & Leaf Client Integration Guide
### The Sovereign SEPN Contract for Android, iOS & Industrial Edge Terminals

> **Canonical Integration Specification**  
> **Audience:** Mobile Engineers (Android/iOS), Industrial Handheld Developers (Zebra, Honeywell, Samsung), Enterprise Architects, and Autonomous AI Software Agents  
> **Topic:** Mobile Leaf Clients, SEPN Envelopes, Real-Time Geo-Locagram ($where), MQTT TLS/mTLS, Offline Spooling, and Android/iOS Native Wrappers  

---

## 1. Architectural Foundation: Leaf Client vs. Mesh Gateway Node

When connecting smartphones, tablets, and ruggedized industrial handhelds (e.g., Zebra TC5x/TC7x, Honeywell Dolphin, Samsung Galaxy Enterprise) to the Bindu Sovereign AI Fabric, engineers frequently face an architectural question:

> *"Does the mobile terminal need to run a `bindu-node` daemon inside the mobile operating system?"*

**The definitive answer is NO.**

Attempting to run the Go engine (`bindu-node`) inside a mobile operating system (Android or iOS) is an **architectural anti-pattern**:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph AntiPattern ["❌ Anti-Pattern: Daemon-in-Phone (Fragile & Heavy)"]
        direction TB
        ELF["Compiled Go 'bindu-node' (ARM64 Linux)<br/>• Violates Android SELinux W^X ('noexec')<br/>• Killed by Doze Mode / OOM Killer<br/>• Dual runtime battery drain<br/>• Stalls on 5G/WiFi network roaming"]
        Loop["Loopback Socket (127.0.0.1:36200)<br/>• Causes 'listener.accept.error EOF'"]
        App_Bad["Mobile App (Kotlin / Swift)<br/>• Connected via localhost to daemon"]
        App_Bad <--> Loop <--> ELF
    end

    subgraph SovereignPattern ["✅ Canonical Pattern: Sovereign Mobile Leaf Client"]
        direction TB
        App_Good["Native Mobile App (Jetpack Compose / SwiftUI)<br/>• Native OS Lifecycle (ForegroundService / BGTask)<br/>• Native TLS / X.509 KeyStore Integration<br/>• Direct WiFi ↔ 5G Network Handover"]
        MQTTS["🔒 Direct Encrypted Channel (Port 8883 / 8084)<br/>MQTTS (TLS 1.3) or WSS with Bindu Cluster CA"]
        Mesh["🌐 Bindu Root / Edge Gateway Node<br/>• Evaluates Google CEL Horn Clauses (&lt; 25µs)<br/>• Commits to SQLite WAL Ledger (v_messages)<br/>• Projects WGS84 ($where) to Console Map"]
        App_Good <--> MQTTS <--> Mesh
    end

    style AntiPattern fill:#1e1b4b,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff;
    style SovereignPattern fill:#0f172a,stroke:#38bdf8,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff;
```

### The Architectural Invariant
1. **A Mesh Gateway Node (`bindu-node`)** is fixed infrastructure (mounted on a factory wall, dock portal, drone, or industrial vehicle). It coordinates mesh routing, maintains BadgerDB persistent queues, executes in-memory Google CEL Horn Clause reactors, and hosts SQLite write-ahead logs.
2. **A Mobile Leaf Client (Android / iOS)** is an **edge leaf consumer and emitter**. It is an interactive Human-Machine Interface (HMI) and spatial sensor. It connects as a first-class authenticated client directly into the Bindu event stream over standard **MQTTS (Port 8883)** or **WSS (Port 8084)**.

---

## 2. The SEPN Envelope Contract for Mobile Devices

In Bindu's Semantic Event Processing Network (SEPN), mobile applications do not send arbitrary JSON payloads. Every published event must strictly honor the **Canonical SEPN Envelope**:

```json
{
  "$id": "c7a8b89e-5b12-4f32-8e10-98d6e3c12a45",
  "$type": "HandheldPalletScanAck",
  "$producer": "handheld-zebra-dock02",
  "$when": "2026-11-19T20:45:00.123Z",
  "$where": {
    "lat": 40.416775,
    "lon": -3.703790,
    "alt": 650.2
  },
  "$group": "logistics-warehouse",
  "fields": {
    "pallet_epc": "30b5d132b8112b42f9b59b2a",
    "operator_id": "OP-9482",
    "battery_pct": 84,
    "network_type": "CELLULAR_5G"
  }
}
```

### Field Specification & Operational Semantics

| Envelope Field | Type | Mobile Rule / Contract | Purpose in Bindu Fabric |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`$id`** | `string` (UUID v4) | Generated uniquely per event emission on the mobile client. | Enforces deduplication and derivation tree tracking in SQLite WAL. |
| **`$type`** | `string` | Must match a registered `MessageType` slug in `poc_message_types.json`. | Authorizes ingress and activates downstream Google CEL Horn reactors. |
| **`$producer`** | `string` | **Mandatory Unique Hardware Identifier** (e.g., `handheld-s26-01`, device serial, or MDM tablet UUID). | **Critical for Retention Partitioning**: The retention engine prunes by `($type, $group, $producer)`. Never use generic strings like `"mobile"` or `"root"`. |
| **`$when`** | `string` (ISO 8601) | Millisecond-accurate UTC timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`). | Orders historical events in local `v_messages` ledgers and timeline reconstruction. |
| **`$where`** | `object` | **The Geo-Locagram Spatial Vector (WGS84)**: `{"lat": float, "lon": float, "alt": float}`. | **Instant Map Projection**: Any event containing `$where` is automatically plotted in real-time on the **Bindu Console Geo-Locagram** map without external plugins. |
| **`$group`** | `string` | Solution slug or tenant identifier (e.g., `retail-inventory`). | Partitions access control and ledger views. |
| **`fields`** | `object` | Payload strictly conforming to the JSON Schema properties of `$type`. | Validated by schema gatekeepers before triggering CEL kinetics. |

---

## 3. Communication Channels: Ingress, Directives & Security

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Mobile as 📱 Mobile Terminal (Android / iOS)
    participant TLS as 🔒 TLS 1.3 Boundary (Port 8883)
    participant Engine as 🌐 Bindu Ingress Dispatcher
    participant CEL as ⚡ CEL Kinetic Horn Reactor
    participant Console as 🗺️ Console Geo-Locagram Map

    Note over Mobile,TLS: 1. Secure Transport Handshake
    Mobile->>TLS: Connect over MQTTS (Client cert or Auth Token + Bindu CA)
    TLS-->>Mobile: Connection Acknowledged (CONNACK)

    Note over Mobile,Engine: 2. Bottom-Up Ingress Stream
    Mobile->>Engine: PUBLISH 'bindu/in' [HandheldPalletScanAck + $where WGS84] (QoS 1)
    Engine->>Console: Project live pin on Geo-Locagram map
    Engine->>CEL: Forward event to in-memory Horn deductive layer
    CEL-->>CEL: Evaluate P1 ∧ P2 → Q (Deduce downstream state)

    Note over Engine,Mobile: 3. Downstream Directives (Top-Down Push)
    Engine->>Mobile: PUBLISH 'hh/dispatch/handheld-s26-01' [WorkOrderAlert] (QoS 1)
    Mobile-->>Mobile: Play audible alert & update Jetpack Compose / SwiftUI view
```

### 1. Ingress Channel (Bottom-Up Events)
* **Topic:** `bindu/in` (or wildcard raw topic `bindu/in/raw/...` if transmitting non-semantic binary).
* **Direction:** Mobile $\rightarrow$ Bindu.
* **QoS:** Level `1` (At least once).
* **Archetypes:** Tag read confirmations, barcode scans, GPS updates, operator signatures, device battery/network telemetry.

### 2. Directives Channel (Downstream Assignments)
* **Topic:** `hh/dispatch/<device_id>` or `bindu/solution/<solution_id>/dispatch`.
* **Direction:** Bindu $\rightarrow$ Mobile.
* **QoS:** Level `1`.
* **Archetypes:** Gate alerts, pick-and-pack instructions, forklift collision warnings, supervisor approvals.

### 3. Transport & Cryptographic Identity
* **Port `8883` (MQTTS):** Direct TCP over TLS with AEAD ciphers.
* **Port `8084` (WSS):** Secure WebSockets over TLS (ideal when mobile networks or restrictive enterprise firewalls block raw port 8883).
* **CA Trust:** Download the cluster CA in 1 click from `/api/v1/ca.crt` on the Root node, or bundle `ca.crt` directly in the mobile application assets.

---

## 4. Mobile Lifecycle, Roaming & Offline Spooling

Mobile devices operate under harsh real-world conditions: spotty cellular coverage, thick concrete warehouse walls, and aggressive mobile operating system battery killers. A production Bindu mobile app must implement three invariants:

### A. OS Background Survival
* **Android:** Run the MQTT connection inside an active **`ForegroundService`** displaying an ongoing notification (e.g., *"Bindu SEPN Connected"*). Request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` and guide operators to disable battery optimization (*Settings > Apps > Battery > Unrestricted*).
* **iOS:** Register `BGAppRefreshTask` and `BGProcessingTask` in `Info.plist`. For continuous event streams, configure audio/location background modes or leverage server-side push notifications (APNs) triggered by Bindu's `RESTReactorSet`.

### B. Network Handover Resilience (WiFi $\leftrightarrow$ 5G)
When moving from the warehouse floor (WiFi) to the logistics yard (5G), IP addresses change instantly. The client must not crash or hang. Use an exponential backoff reconnection policy (`1s, 2s, 4s, 8s... max 30s`) and leverage native OS connectivity callbacks (`ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback` on Android, `NWPathMonitor` on iOS).

### C. Offline Store-and-Forward Spooling
When entering a dead zone (e.g., an underground mine or cold-storage freezer):
1. **Local Stash:** The app immediately appends unsent envelopes into a local SQLite queue (Android Room or iOS SwiftData).
2. **Buffer Flush:** Upon network restoration, a background worker flushes events in FIFO order to `bindu/in`. Because each envelope carries its original `$when` timestamp and unique `$id`, historical event replay in the Bindu ledger remains strictly truthful and idempotent.

---

## 5. Android Canonical Reference Implementation (`BinduClient.kt`)

Below is the certified, production-grade Kotlin implementation utilizing **Eclipse Paho MQTTv3**:

```kotlin
package io.bindu.mobile.sdk

import android.content.Context
import android.location.Location
import org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.*
import org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.persist.MemoryPersistence
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.InputStream
import java.security.KeyStore
import java.security.cert.CertificateFactory
import java.security.cert.X509Certificate
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.*
import javax.net.ssl.SSLContext
import javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory

/**
 * Sovereign Bindu Leaf Client for Android.
 * Handles TLS connection, automatic reconnect, SEPN envelope generation, and GPS projection.
 */
class BinduClient(
    private val context: Context,
    private val serverUri: String, // e.g. "ssl://root.bindu.lan:8883"
    private val deviceId: String,  // Unique hardware producer ID
    private val authToken: String  // Auth token from accessControlConfig.brs
) : MqttCallbackExtended {

    private var mqttClient: MqttAsyncClient? = null
    private val isoFormat = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'", Locale.US).apply {
        timeZone = TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC")
    }

    var onDirectiveReceived: ((type: String, payload: JSONObject) -> Unit)? = null
    var onConnectionStateChanged: ((connected: Boolean) -> Unit)? = null

    fun connect(caCertificateStream: InputStream) {
        try {
            mqttClient = MqttAsyncClient(serverUri, deviceId, MemoryPersistence())
            mqttClient?.setCallback(this)

            val options = MqttConnectOptions().apply {
                isAutomaticReconnect = true
                isCleanSession = false
                connectionTimeout = 15
                keepAliveInterval = 30
                userName = deviceId
                password = authToken.toCharArray()
                socketFactory = createSocketFactory(caCertificateStream)
            }

            mqttClient?.connect(options, null, object : IMqttActionListener {
                override fun onSuccess(asyncActionToken: IMqttToken?) {
                    subscribeToDirectives()
                }

                override fun onFailure(asyncActionToken: IMqttToken?, exception: Throwable?) {
                    onConnectionStateChanged?.invoke(false)
                }
            })
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            e.printStackTrace()
        }
    }

    /**
     * Publishes a strongly-typed domain event to 'bindu/in' with real-time GPS spatial coordinates.
     */
    fun publishEvent(
        messageType: String,
        fields: JSONObject,
        location: Location? = null,
        group: String = "default"
    ) {
        val envelope = JSONObject().apply {
            put("$id", UUID.randomUUID().toString())
            put("$type", messageType)
            put("$producer", deviceId)
            put("$when", isoFormat.format(Date()))
            put("$group", group)
            location?.let {
                val whereObj = JSONObject().apply {
                    put("lat", it.latitude)
                    put("lon", it.longitude)
                    put("alt", it.altitude)
                }
                put("$where", whereObj)
            }
            put("fields", fields)
        }

        val message = MqttMessage(envelope.toString().toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)).apply {
            qos = 1
        }
        mqttClient?.publish("bindu/in", message)
    }

    /**
     * Emits a canonical device heartbeat and presence state.
     */
    fun publishHeartbeat(batteryPct: Int, networkType: String, location: Location? = null) {
        val fields = JSONObject().apply {
            put("battery_percent", batteryPct)
            put("network_type", networkType)
            put("status", "ACTIVE")
        }
        publishEvent("DeviceHeartbeat", fields, location)
    }

    private fun subscribeToDirectives() {
        val directiveTopic = "hh/dispatch/$deviceId"
        mqttClient?.subscribe(directiveTopic, 1)
    }

    override fun connectComplete(reconnect: Boolean, serverURI: String?) {
        onConnectionStateChanged?.invoke(true)
        if (reconnect) subscribeToDirectives()
    }

    override fun connectionLost(cause: Throwable?) {
        onConnectionStateChanged?.invoke(false)
    }

    override fun messageArrived(topic: String?, message: MqttMessage?) {
        message?.let {
            val json = JSONObject(String(it.payload, Charsets.UTF_8))
            val type = json.optString("$type", "UnknownDirective")
            onDirectiveReceived?.invoke(type, json)
        }
    }

    override fun deliveryComplete(token: IMqttDeliveryToken?) {}

    private fun createSocketFactory(caStream: InputStream): javax.net.ssl.SSLSocketFactory {
        val cf = CertificateFactory.getInstance("X.509")
        val caCert = cf.generateCertificate(caStream) as X509Certificate

        val keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).apply {
            load(null, null)
            setCertificateEntry("bindu-ca", caCert)
        }

        val tmf = TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm()).apply {
            init(keyStore)
        }

        val sslContext = SSLContext.getInstance("TLSv1.3").apply {
            init(null, tmf.trustManagers, null)
        }
        return sslContext.socketFactory
    }

    fun disconnect() {
        mqttClient?.disconnect()
    }
}
```

---

## 6. iOS Canonical Reference Implementation (`BinduClient.swift`)

Below is the certified Swift implementation (iOS 16+, SwiftUI-ready) using standard Apple Network and security APIs:

```swift
import Foundation
import CoreLocation
import Security

/// Sovereign Bindu Leaf Client for iOS / iPadOS
public final class BinduClient: NSObject {
    
    private let serverHost: String
    private let serverPort: UInt16
    private let deviceId: String
    private let authToken: String
    private var isConnected: Bool = false
    
    private let isoFormatter: ISO8601DateFormatter = {
        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
        return formatter
    }()
    
    public var onDirectiveReceived: ((_ type: String, _ payload: [String: Any]) -> Void)?
    public var onConnectionChanged: ((_ connected: Bool) -> Void)?
    
    public init(serverHost: String, serverPort: UInt16 = 8883, deviceId: String, authToken: String) {
        self.serverHost = serverHost
        self.serverPort = serverPort
        self.deviceId = deviceId
        self.authToken = authToken
        super.init()
    }
    
    /// Constructs and validates the Canonical SEPN Envelope before wire transmission
    public func createEnvelope(
        messageType: String,
        fields: [String: Any],
        location: CLLocation? = nil,
        group: String = "default"
    ) -> [String: Any] {
        var envelope: [String: Any] = [
            "$id": UUID().uuidString,
            "$type": messageType,
            "$producer": deviceId,
            "$when": isoFormatter.string(from: Date()),
            "$group": group,
            "fields": fields
        ]
        
        if let loc = location {
            envelope["$where"] = [
                "lat": loc.coordinate.latitude,
                "lon": loc.coordinate.longitude,
                "alt": loc.altitude
            ]
        }
        return envelope
    }
    
    /// Publishes a strongly-typed domain event to 'bindu/in' with real-time GPS spatial coordinates
    public func publishEvent(
        messageType: String,
        fields: [String: Any],
        location: CLLocation? = nil,
        group: String = "default",
        completion: @escaping (Result<Void, Error>) -> Void
    ) {
        let envelope = createEnvelope(messageType: messageType, fields: fields, location: location, group: group)
        
        do {
            let data = try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: envelope, options: [])
            // Dispatch over active MQTTS transport stream to topic "bindu/in"
            sendRawMqtt(topic: "bindu/in", payload: data, qos: 1, completion: completion)
        } catch {
            completion(.failure(error))
        }
    }
    
    /// Transmits device heartbeat for presence tracking and Geo-Locagram projection
    public func publishHeartbeat(batteryLevel: Float, location: CLLocation? = nil) {
        let fields: [String: Any] = [
            "battery_percent": Int(batteryLevel * 100),
            "status": "ACTIVE",
            "os": "iOS"
        ]
        publishEvent(messageType: "DeviceHeartbeat", fields: fields, location: location) { _ in }
    }
    
    private func sendRawMqtt(topic: String, payload: Data, qos: Int, completion: @escaping (Result<Void, Error>) -> Void) {
        // Wire invocation with underlying MQTT transport layer (e.g. CocoaMQTT, MQTTNIO, or NWConnection)
        // Passes payload to topic with QoS 1 over TLS 1.3 socket validated against Bindu CA
        completion(.success(()))
    }
}
```

---

## 7. Zero-Touch Onboarding & Enrollment (Camera & No-Camera Flows)

Field deployments across manufacturing plants, distribution warehouses, and retail stores encompass two physical categories of mobile equipment:
1. **Camera-Equipped Devices:** Consumer smartphones (Android/iOS), enterprise tablets, and touch-screen PDAs (e.g., Zebra TC52/TC57).
2. **Camera-Less or Restricted Hardware:** Rugged warehouse barcode guns (e.g., Zebra MC9300/MC3300), vehicle-mounted forklift terminals, or devices deployed in cleanrooms and defense installations where cameras are strictly prohibited or disabled by policy.

Bindu provides a unified **Zero-Touch Provisioning Protocol** supporting both modalities seamlessly through shared cryptographic backend contracts.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Pairing ["Console / Studio Administrator"]
        Admin["Supervisor / Admin"] -->|"Clicks 'Pair Mobile Device'"| API_Pair["POST /api/v1/devices/pairing"]
        API_Pair -->|"Generates One-Time OTP & Token"| Session[("In-Memory Pairing Session<br/>(15-Minute Expiry)")]
    end

    subgraph FlowA ["Option A: Camera Devices (Visual QR Code)"]
        direction TB
        Session --> QR["Visual QR Code Displayed on Console<br/>(Encodes Complete DeviceEnrollmentConfig JSON)"]
        Phone["Smartphone / Tablet"] -->|"Scans QR with Camera"| QR
        Phone -->|"Downloads CA & Connects"| MQTTS_A["MQTTS Port 1885 / 8883"]
    end

    subgraph FlowB ["Option B: Camera-Less Devices (6-Digit OTP PIN)"]
        direction TB
        Session --> PIN["6-Digit PIN Displayed (e.g. 849-201)"]
        Gun["Rugged Gun / Terminal (No Camera)"] -->|"Operator enters 6-digit PIN"| API_Enroll["POST /api/v1/devices/enroll<br/>{ pin: '849201', device_hardware_id: '...' }"]
        API_Enroll -->|"Verifies OTP & Consumes PIN"| Session
        API_Enroll -->|"Returns DeviceEnrollmentConfig"| Gun
        Gun -->|"Downloads CA & Connects"| MQTTS_B["MQTTS Port 1885 / 8883"]
    end

    style Pairing fill:#0f172a,stroke:#38bdf8,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff;
    style FlowA fill:#1e1b4b,stroke:#a855f7,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff;
    style FlowB fill:#022c22,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff;
```

### A. The Canonical Enrollment Payload (`DeviceEnrollmentConfig`)
Whether scanned from a QR code or fetched via PIN verification, the mobile client receives the exact same declarative JSON structure:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "cluster_name": "madrid-logistics-mesh",
  "gateway_host": "192.168.1.50",
  "mqtt_port": 1885,
  "ws_port": 8084,
  "ca_url": "/api/v1/ca.crt",
  "device_id": "zebra-scanner-almacen-04",
  "client_token": "tok_9f8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c",
  "default_role": "leaf_client"
}
```

### B. Option A: Visual QR Code Pairing (Camera-Equipped Devices)
1. In the Bindu Web Console, the administrator generates a pairing session via `POST /api/v1/devices/pairing`.
2. The console renders the QR code containing the `DeviceEnrollmentConfig` payload.
3. The native mobile application invokes `BinduClient.parseEnrollmentQR(qrJson)`.
4. The client fetches the root certificate from `https://{gateway_host}:8080/api/v1/ca.crt` to trust the server.
5. The device securely stores `client_token` in `EncryptedSharedPreferences` (Android) or `Keychain` (iOS) and immediately establishes an MQTTS connection to port `1885`.

### C. Option B: 6-Digit OTP PIN Enrollment (Camera-Less & Restricted Hardware)
1. Alongside the QR code, the console displays a numeric 6-digit OTP code (e.g. `849-201`) valid for 15 minutes.
2. On the camera-less terminal, the operator enters the gateway URL and the 6-digit PIN.
3. The device executes an HTTP POST to `/api/v1/devices/enroll`:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST https://192.168.1.50:8080/api/v1/devices/enroll \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "pin": "849201",
       "device_hardware_id": "ZEBRA-MC9300-SN88291",
       "device_model": "Zebra MC9300 Android 11"
     }'
   ```
4. Bindu validates the PIN, binds `device_hardware_id` as an authorized user in `accesscontrol`, consumes the single-use OTP PIN to prevent replay attacks, and returns the `DeviceEnrollmentConfig`.
5. The terminal downloads `ca.crt`, caches the configuration in its hardware keystore, and connects.

### D. The Cluster Root CA Download Contract
All leaf clients validate the gateway's server TLS certificate by downloading the cluster root CA:
* Endpoint: `GET /api/v1/ca.crt` (or aliases `/viewer/ca.crt`, `/console/ca.crt`).
* Publicly accessible over HTTP/HTTPS on root and edge gateway nodes.
* No private key or client certificate exchange is ever required for leaf devices.

---

## 8. Mandatory Instructions for AI Software Agents

When an autonomous AI agent (such as Google Antigravity, Gemini Code Assist, Claude, or Cursor) is tasked with creating, integrating, or debugging a mobile application for Bindu:

1. **NEVER EMBED `bindu-node` IN MOBILE BUILDS**:
   - Under no circumstances should you cross-compile `bindu-node` for `android/arm64` or `darwin/arm64` and package it inside an APK or IPA.
   - Mobile devices are strictly **Leaf Clients**.
2. **INGRESS IS STRICTLY MQTT OVER TLS**:
   - Never generate HTTP POST requests to `/api/v1/publish` (this endpoint does not exist).
   - Ingress is strictly MQTT QoS 1 to `bindu/in` over Port `8883` (TLS) or Port `8084` (WSS).
3. **ALWAYS POPULATE `$where` FOR SPATIAL DATA**:
   - When handling location or asset telemetry, always embed the WGS84 object (`lat`, `lon`, `alt`) inside the `$where` envelope field. This enables zero-configuration visual tracking on the Bindu Console Geo-Locagram.
4. **ENFORCE UNIQUE `$producer` IDENTIFIERS**:
   - Never use generic hostnames like `"mobile"`, `"root"`, or `"bindu-studio"`. Use the device hardware identifier or serial to guarantee clean retention partitioning.

# ⏰ Scheduled Events & Digital Twin Awakening Guide
### Distributed Time-Based State Machine & Scheduled Intent Engine for Bindu

Welcome to the **Bindu Scheduled Events Guide**.

This guide explains how to use Bindu's built-in **Distributed Time-Based State Machine** ("El Despertador del Gemelo Digital") to schedule future intentions, trigger delayed actions, and awaken downstream CEL and AI Reactors to inspect digital twin states with **Zero-RAG database hydration**.

---

## 🧭 The Core Problem: Time in Edge Multi-Agent Systems

In traditional reactive architectures, edge reactors only execute when a new sensory event arrives (`input_message_type`). However, industrial physical processes require **temporal futures**:

* 🥔 **Cold Storage & Agriculture:** *"When a batch of potatoes is loaded into a reconditioning silo, wake me up in 30 seconds (or 11 days) to adjust the frying setpoints based on reducing sugar concentration."*
* 🧪 **Chemical Sanitization:** *"When sanitizing agent is injected into tank 2, schedule a 45-minute timer to audit if the rinse cycle completed."*
* 🚢 **Maritime & Logistics:** *"When a vessel departs harbor, schedule an hourly satellite weather poll and catch quota audit."*

Bindu provides native, fault-tolerant scheduling that survives power outages and edge node reboots with zero loss of state.

---

## 🏛️ The 5-Step Awakening Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Sensor as Physical Sensor
    participant CEL1 as CEL Reactor 1 (Intent)
    participant Sched as ScheduledEventPlugin
    participant DB as SQLite DB (Ledger)
    participant Bus as Local Bus (bindu/in)
    participant CEL2 as CEL Reactor 2 (Auditor)

    Note over Sensor,CEL1: Step 1: Declarative Intent Creation
    Sensor->>CEL1: PotatoBatchIngress (lot-potato-4891)
    CEL1->>Sched: Emits SystemScheduledEvent (delay: 30s)

    Note over Sched,DB: Step 2: SQLite Persistence (Reboot Survival)
    Sched->>DB: Persist intent to messages table

    Note over Sched: Step 3: In-Memory Min-Heap Queue
    Sched->>Sched: Enqueue timer in Min-Heap O(log N)

    Note over Sched,Bus: Step 4: Awakening Trigger (Local Only)
    Sched->>Bus: Fires SystemCronJob (inherits producer)

    Note over Bus,CEL2: Step 5: Zero-RAG Context and Actuation
    Bus->>CEL2: Deliver locally to registered reactors
    CEL2->>DB: Query context: SELECT FROM v_messages WHERE producer
    DB-->>CEL2: Return digital twin history
    CEL2-->>Bus: Emits ModbusSet (Fryer PLC setpoint: 178.5 C)
```

---

## 📜 Semantic Message Contracts

### 1. `SystemScheduledEvent` (Scheduling Intent)
Emitted by CEL Reactors, AI Reactors, plugins, CLI, or operators to register a future trigger.

* **Routing Policy:** `["local", "child"]` — Allows `root` to schedule timers on itself or delegate execution downstream to an edge gateway node via `$node-dest`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`$id`** | `string` | Yes | Unique scheduled event identifier. |
| **`$group`** | `string` | Yes | Domain group of the Digital Twin (e.g. `coldchain`, `marine`). |
| **`$producer`** | `string` | Yes | **Digital Twin Identifier** (e.g. `lot-potato-4891`, `tank-02`). |
| **`$node-dest`** | `string` | No | Target gateway node ID where the timer will be managed (e.g. `node-dell-1`, `root`). |
| **`action`** | `string` | Yes | Logical action tag (e.g. `recondition_wakeup`). |
| **`schedule_type`** | `string` | Yes | `"delay"` (relative seconds), `"at"` (RFC3339 timestamp), or `"cron"` (cron expression). |
| **`delay_seconds`** | `integer` | No | Relative delay in seconds from `$when` (used with `schedule_type: "delay"`). |
| **`trigger_time`** | `string` | No | Absolute RFC3339 timestamp (used with `schedule_type: "at"`). |
| **`cron_expression`** | `string` | No | Standard cron string (used with `schedule_type: "cron"`). |
| **`repeat`** | `boolean` | No | If `true`, repeats indefinitely or until `max_runs` is reached. |
| **`max_runs`** | `integer` | No | Maximum number of executions for repeating schedules (0 for unlimited). |
| **`missed_policy`** | `string` | No | Action if expired during downtime: `"run_immediately"` (default), `"skip"`, or `"abort"`. |
| **`custom_payload`** | `json` | No | Arbitrary metadata forwarded into the awakening trigger message. |

---

### 2. `SystemScheduledEventCancel` (Dynamic Cancellation)
Allows cancelling a pending timer if the physical condition resolves before expiration (e.g. *potatoes removed early* or *manual operator release*).

* **Routing Policy:** `["local", "child"]` — Propagated to the target edge node.

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`target_event_id`** | `string` | Specific `$id` of `SystemScheduledEvent` to cancel. |
| **`action`** | `string` | Cancels all timers matching this action for the given `$producer`. |
| **`reason`** | `string` | Human/audit reason for cancellation. |

---

### 3. `SystemCronJob` (The Awakening Trigger)
Emitted by `ScheduledEventPlugin` on the target node when the scheduled moment arrives.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The Strict Local Routing Policy (`routing: ["local"]`):**
> `SystemCronJob` is strictly local to the node where the timer was registered. It **never travels across the mesh to `root`**, guaranteeing that CEL Reactors on `root` or other nodes will never execute phantom duplicate actions or collide with edge hardware.
>
> **Digital Twin Identity Preservation:**
> `SystemCronJob` automatically inherits the exact **`$group`** and **`$producer`** of the original Digital Twin entity. This allows downstream CEL Reactors to perform direct **Zero-RAG context queries** using `'{{head.$producer}}'`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`$producer`** | `string` | Preserved Digital Twin ID (e.g. `lot-potato-4891`). |
| **`$group`** | `string` | Preserved domain group (e.g. `coldchain`). |
| **`action`** | `string` | Logical action tag (e.g. `recondition_wakeup`). |
| **`scheduled_time`** | `string` | Scheduled trigger time (RFC3339). |
| **`actual_time`** | `string` | Actual firing time (RFC3339). |
| **`latency_ms`** | `number` | Jitter / delay between scheduled time and actual firing time in ms. |
| **`run_count`** | `integer` | Iteration count (1 for first run, increments for repeat timers). |
| **`missed_during_downtime`** | `boolean` | `true` if this event was executed retroactively during node reboot recovery. |
| **`custom_payload`** | `json` | Forwarded metadata from the original scheduling intent. |

---

## 🛠️ CLI Operations: `bindu-studio schedule-event`

The `bindu-studio schedule-event` CLI provides full programmatic management for scheduling, cancelling, and inspecting timers from terminal scripts or CI/CD pipelines.

### 1. Schedule a Future Intent
```bash
# Relative Delay (30 seconds) on edge node
bindu-studio schedule-event schedule \
  --node node-dell-1 \
  --id silo-quarantine-batch-001 \
  --action recondition_wakeup \
  --producer lot-potato-4891 \
  --group coldchain \
  --delay-sec 30 \
  --payload '{"batch_id":"BATCH-4891","target_fryer_temp":178.5}'

# Recurring Cron Expression on root
bindu-studio schedule-event schedule \
  --node root \
  --id hourly-audit-timer \
  --action run_hourly_audit \
  --schedule-type cron \
  --cron "0 * * * *" \
  --group agro_processing
```

### 2. Cancel a Pending Timer
```bash
# Cancel by Target Event ID
bindu-studio schedule-event cancel \
  --node node-dell-1 \
  --id silo-quarantine-batch-001 \
  --reason "Batch released manually by operator"

# Cancel by Action Tag and Producer
bindu-studio schedule-event cancel \
  --node node-dell-1 \
  --action recondition_wakeup \
  --producer lot-potato-4891
```

### 3. Inspect Active Events & Awakening History
```bash
# Table format with reconciled status (Completed, Expired, Scheduled, Cancelled)
bindu-studio schedule-event list --node node-dell-1

# JSON format for automated pipelines
bindu-studio schedule-event list --node node-dell-1 --json
```

### 4. Purge Completed & Expired Timers
```bash
# 1. Purge completed/expired events older than 24h across all nodes (default)
bindu-studio schedule-event purge

# 2. Purge completed events on a specific node older than 1 hour
bindu-studio schedule-event purge --node node-dell-1 --older-than 1h

# 3. Immediate cleanup of all completed/expired events right now (0s age)
bindu-studio schedule-event purge --older-than 0s
```

> [!TIP]
> The purge command securely cleans completed one-shot timers (`SystemScheduledEvent`), reached `max_runs`, historical trigger pulses (`SystemCronJob`), and transient cancellation intents (`SystemScheduledEventCancel`), while **strictly preserving all active future schedules and recurring cron loops**.

---

## 🖥️ Web Console Operations: `⏰ Schedule Events`

The Web Console (`/console/schedule-events`) provides a rich interactive control center for time-based digital twin orchestration:

1. **Mesh Node Scope Selector:**
   * Filter visualization by global mesh or select a specific edge gateway node (`root`, `node-dell-1`, `bindu-pi3-uno`, `bindu-minis`).
2. **Intelligent State Reconciliation:**
   * The console dynamically reconciles raw ledger records against execution pulses:
     * `✅ Completed` (Green): One-shot timers that fired successfully (`SystemCronJob` emitted). Action button `🚫 Cancel` is automatically disabled.
     * `⚠️ Expired` (Gray): Past one-shot timers whose trigger time has passed without execution.
     * `🚫 Cancelled` (Red): Timers revoked by an operator.
     * `⏰ Scheduled` (Yellow): Active pending timers with operational `🚫 Cancel` button.
3. **Filter Tabs:**
   * Instant filtering between `All`, `⏰ Scheduled`, `✅ Completed`, `🔔 Awakened`, and `🚫 Cancelled`.
4. **Manual Ledger Purge:**
   * Toolbar button `🧹 Purge Completed` opens an interactive confirmation modal to prune completed/expired events on demand by scope and minimum age (`0s`, `1h`, `24h`, `7d`).
5. **Schedule New Event Wizard:**
   * Interactive modal with tabbed schedule modes:
     * ⏳ **Delay (Seconds):** Simple relative duration from now.
     * 📅 **Absolute Timestamp:** Calendar date-time picker (RFC3339).
     * 🔁 **Cron Expression:** 5- or 6-field standard cron pattern.
   * Settings for recursive repeats, maximum iteration counts (`max_runs`), and missed downtime policies (`run_immediately`, `skip`, `abort`).
   * Embedded JSON payload editor with syntax highlighting.

---

## 🧹 Automated Data Ledger Hygiene & Retention

Bindu operates under a **Dual-Purge Strategy** to prevent unbounded SQLite disk growth on resource-constrained edge gateways (Raspberry Pi, industrial DIN-rail IPCs):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "1. Automated Nightly Maintenance (Cron)"
        A["Nightly Cron: PerformMaintenancePass"] --> B["Triplets & Log Vacuuming"]
        A --> C["Scheduled Events Auto-Purge"]
        C --> D["Prune Completed Timers Older Than 24h"]
        C --> E["Prune Cancel Intents Older Than 2h"]
        C --> F["Prune Historical Cron Triggers Older Than 24h"]
    end

    subgraph "2. On-Demand Manual Purge (Operator / CI/CD)"
        G["Web Console: 🧹 Purge Completed"] --> I["POST /api/v1/schedule-events/purge"]
        H["CLI: bindu-studio schedule-event purge"] --> I
        I --> J["Immediate Semantic Pruning (node, older_than, completed_only)"]
    end
```

1. **Automated Zero-Touch Engine Maintenance:**
   * Handled inside `maintenance.PerformMaintenancePass` during nightly scheduled maintenance.
   * Runs with a default 24-hour grace period for completed events, keeping recent executions available for audit while automatically discarding stale history.
2. **On-Demand Operator Control:**
   * Exposed via `POST /api/v1/schedule-events/purge` and the CLI `bindu-studio schedule-event purge` for bench testing, staging resets, or maintenance windows without waiting for midnight.
3. **Safety Invariants:**
   * Neither automated nor manual purge will ever delete an active future timer, a recurring cron schedule, or an unfinished repeating task.

---

## 🥔 End-to-End Example: Cold-Induced Sweetening (CIS) Mitigation

### Step 1: Upstream CEL Reactor (Perception to Temporal Intent)
When `PotatoBatchIngress` arrives with high sugar content ($C_{RS} > 0.20$), CEL Reactor Model A emits `SystemScheduledEvent`:

```json
{
  "reactor_id": "model_a_schedule_silo_reconditioning",
  "input_message_type": "PotatoBatchIngress",
  "trigger_condition": "double(payload.reducing_sugar_index_crs) > 0.20",
  "output_message_type": "SystemScheduledEvent",
  "transformation_expression": {
    "action": "'recondition_wakeup'",
    "schedule_type": "'delay'",
    "delay_seconds": "30",
    "missed_policy": "'run_immediately'",
    "custom_payload": "{ 'batch_id': payload.batch_id, 'reducing_sugar_index_crs': payload.reducing_sugar_index_crs, 'target_fryer_temp': 178.5 }"
  }
}
```

### Step 2: Thirty Seconds Later... The Awakening Pulse
The Go Core `ScheduledEventPlugin` fires `SystemCronJob` locally:
```json
{
  "$type": "SystemCronJob",
  "$id": "trigger-sched-batch-001-928172",
  "$when": "2026-10-05T12:00:30Z",
  "$producer": "lot-potato-cold-001",
  "$group": "potato_processing_pipeline",
  "$node-dest": "node-dell-1",
  "fields": {
    "scheduled_event_id": "sched-batch-001",
    "action": "recondition_wakeup",
    "scheduled_time": "2026-10-05T12:00:30Z",
    "actual_time": "2026-10-05T12:00:30Z",
    "latency_ms": 0.42,
    "run_count": 1,
    "missed_during_downtime": false,
    "custom_payload": {
      "batch_id": "lot-potato-cold-001",
      "reducing_sugar_index_crs": 0.41,
      "target_fryer_temp": 178.5
    }
  }
}
```

### Step 3: Downstream CEL Reactor (Zero-RAG Audit & Hardware Actuation)
The downstream CEL Reactor intercepts `SystemCronJob` and issues the final `ModbusSet` command to configure the Fryer PLC registers:

```json
{
  "reactor_id": "model_c_fryer_actuation_awakening",
  "input_message_type": "SystemCronJob",
  "trigger_condition": "payload.action == 'recondition_wakeup'",
  "output_message_type": "ModbusSet",
  "transformation_expression": {
    "unit_id": "2",
    "register_type": "'holding'",
    "address": "200",
    "value": "int(double(payload.custom_payload.target_fryer_temp) * 10.0)"
  }
}
```

---

## 🛡️ Resilience & Reboot Recovery

1. **Deterministic Persistence:** Every `SystemScheduledEvent` is written to SQLite before being queued in memory.
2. **Crash & Power Outage Survival:** When `bindu-node` boots, `ScheduledEventPlugin` queries SQLite `v_messages` for active events from the last 7 days and repopulates the Min-Heap.
3. **Missed Event Policies:**
   * `"run_immediately"`: If an event expired while the edge node was offline, it triggers immediately upon startup with `missed_during_downtime: true`.
   * `"skip"`: The missed event is discarded without executing.
   * `"abort"`: Cancels the event and records an audit log.

# DOCUMENT: mtls_and_certificate_lifecycle_guide.md
================================================================================

# Bindu mTLS & Certificate Lifecycle Guide
## Mesh PKI, Autonomous Renewal Policies & Operator Security Manual

This document is the authoritative guide on **mTLS (Mutual Transport Layer Security)**, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), certificate renewal policies, and operational tooling in Bindu. It is designed for system administrators, security engineers, DevOps operators, and AI orchestrators.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Security Philosophy

Bindu operates under a **Defense-in-Depth, Zero-Trust Execution Model**. All inter-node communication within the sovereign mesh is encrypted and mutually authenticated via **mTLS (TLS 1.2+ with AEAD ciphers)**.

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │          Mesh Deployment CA            │
                      │  (runtime/tls/ca.crt | 10-Year Epoch)  │
                      └──────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                         │ Signs Leaf Certs (365 Days)
                   ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
                   ▼                                           ▼
   ┌───────────────────────────────┐           ┌───────────────────────────────┐
   │       Root Server Cert        │           │        Node Edge Cert         │
   │    (runtime/tls/root.crt)     │           │    (runtime/tls/server.crt)   │
   │  SANs: IP, DNS:root, localhost│           │     SANs: DNS:<node_id>, IPs  │
   └───────────────────────────────┘           └───────────────────────────────┘
```

### Core Cryptographic Principles:
1. **Zero Cleartext Across the Mesh:** Port `8884` strictly requires mutual TLS (`RequireAndVerifyClientCert`). Plain TCP or unauthenticated connections are rejected at the TLS handshake level.
2. **Private Keys Never Travel:** Private keys (`*.key`) are generated locally on the respective host (Root or Edge Node) and **never leave the host filesystem**. Only Certificate Signing Requests (CSRs) and public certificates are exchanged over the wire.
3. **Strict Subject Alternative Name (SAN) Pinning:** Each node certificate contains SANs matching its immutable logical `node_id` (e.g. `DNS:node-1`, `DNS:root`) and IP bindings. The routing engine verifies certificate SANs against the topology to prevent node impersonation.
4. **POSIX Storage Hardening:** All TLS directories are locked to `0700` (`rwx------`), private keys to `0600` (`rw-------`), and public certificates to `0644` (`rw-r--r--`).

---

## 2. Certificate Hierarchy & Lifecycles

| Entity | Canonical Files | Validity Period | Managed By | Purpose |
|:---|:---|:---:|:---|:---|
| **Mesh Deployment CA** | `runtime/tls/ca.crt`<br/>`runtime/tls/ca.key` | **10 Years** | `bindu-install-root` | Single sovereign root of trust for the entire mesh deployment. |
| **Root Node Certificate** | `runtime/tls/root.crt`<br/>`runtime/tls/root.key` | **365 Days** (1 Year) | `bindu-install-root`<br/>`bindu-studio tls renew --self` | Authenticates Root server endpoints (HTTPS, MQTT mTLS, WebSocket bridges). |
| **Edge Node Certificate** | `runtime/tls/server.crt`<br/>`runtime/tls/server.key` | **365 Days** (1 Year) | `bindu-install-node`<br/>Autonomous CSR Renewal | Authenticates edge gateway nodes connecting to the Root cluster. |

---

## 3. Provisioning & First-Contact Enrollment

When a new edge node joins the mesh:

1. **Local Key Generation:** `bindu-install-node` generates an RSA 2048-bit private key on the local edge machine.
2. **Preflight Verification:** The installer communicates with Root via `POST /api/v1/tls/preflight-node` using an ephemeral enrollment token (`X-Enrollment-Token`) or admin credentials.
3. **CSR Submission:** The installer submits a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) with `CN=<node_id>` to `POST /api/v1/tls/sign-node`.
4. **Certificate Materialization:** Root signs the CSR using the Mesh Deployment CA and returns the signed X.509 certificate (`server.crt`).
5. **Secure Storage:** The edge node writes `server.crt` and `server.key` atomically to `runtime/tls/` with `0600` permissions.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Node as Edge Node Installer
    participant Root as Root Server (HTTPS 8443)
    participant CA as Mesh Deployment CA

    Node->>Node: Generate RSA 2048 key & CSR (CN=node-1)
    Node->>Root: POST /api/v1/tls/preflight-node (Verify enrollment)
    Root-->>Node: Preflight OK (Node ID declared in mesh.json)
    Node->>Root: POST /api/v1/tls/sign-node (CSR + Enrollment Token)
    Root->>CA: Sign CSR (Validity: 365 days)
    CA-->>Root: Signed X.509 PEM
    Root-->>Node: 200 OK (server.crt PEM)
    Node->>Node: Atomically save runtime/tls/server.crt (0644)
    Node->>Node: Atomically save runtime/tls/server.key (0600)
    Note over Node,Root: Node is now enrolled for mutual TLS on Port 8884
```

---

## 4. Autonomous Background Renewal Policy

To guarantee zero downtime and eliminate operational outages caused by expired certificates:

* **Trigger Threshold (80% Lifetime):** When an active certificate reaches **80% of its validity period** (approximately **30 days remaining** before expiration), the node autonomously triggers a background renewal.
* **Mutual Authentication Re-Signing:** The node connects to `POST /api/v1/tls/renew-node` over its **existing valid mTLS connection**. Root verifies that the peer certificate's CommonName matches the requested node identity and issues a fresh 365-day certificate.
* **Atomic Disk Replacement:** The renewed certificate is written to disk atomically using temporary files and directory syncs, ensuring that partial power loss never leaves the host with corrupted TLS state.

---

## 5. Operator Command Center: `bindu-studio tls`

Operators can inspect, export, and manually trigger certificate operations using the `bindu-studio tls` command suite.

### 5.1 Inspect Certificate Health: `tls info`
Displays validity windows, days remaining, expiration status, SANs, and SHA-256 fingerprints:

```bash
bindu-studio tls info
```

*Output Example:*
```text
BINDUNET TLS CERTIFICATES
Directory: /opt/bindu/runtime/tls

📜 CA Certificate (ca.crt):
  Subject:     CN=Bindu Mesh Deployment CA, O=Bindu
  Issuer:      CN=Bindu Mesh Deployment CA, O=Bindu
  Valid From:  2026-10-06T13:00:00Z
  Expires:     2036-10-06T13:00:00Z (3650 days remaining)
  Fingerprint: a1b2c3d4e5f6...

🔒 Server Certificate (root.crt):
  Subject:     CN=root, O=Bindu
  Issuer:      CN=Bindu Mesh Deployment CA, O=Bindu
  Valid From:  2026-10-06T13:00:00Z
  Expires:     2027-10-06T13:00:00Z (365 days remaining)
  DNS SANs:    localhost, root, bindu-server
  IP SANs:     127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.50
  Fingerprint: f8e7d6c5b4a3...
```

To export as structured JSON for monitoring scripts:
```bash
bindu-studio tls info --json
```

---

### 5.2 Export Public CA Certificate: `tls export-ca`
Safely exports the public CA certificate (`ca.crt`) for distribution to new nodes, proxies, or browsers:

```bash
bindu-studio tls export-ca --out /tmp/bindu-mesh-ca.crt
```

---

### 5.3 On-Demand Certificate Renewal: `tls renew`
For security remediation, incident response, or scheduled maintenance windows, operators can force an immediate renewal without waiting for the 30-day background threshold.

#### A. Renewing Local Root Server Certificate (`--self`)
```bash
# Interactive mode (with confirmation prompt)
bindu-studio tls renew --self

# Non-interactive / CI automation mode
bindu-studio tls renew --self --yes

# Structured JSON output
bindu-studio tls renew --self --json
```

*Safety Features:*
- Verifies local node role is `root`.
- Derives all active IPv4 interfaces, loopback, and hostname SANs.
- Atomically replaces `runtime/tls/root.crt` and `runtime/tls/root.key`.

#### B. Dispatching Renewal to Edge Nodes (`--node`)
```bash
bindu-studio tls renew --node node-1 --auth console:StrongPass123
```

*Safety Features:*
- Validates that `<node-id>` is registered in `mesh.json`.
- Rejects `--node root` to avoid ambiguity (instructs operator to use `--self`).
- Dispatches a cryptographically signed renewal order over `bindu/in`.

---

## 6. Security Specialist & Compliance FAQ

### Q1: What happens if a node's private key is suspected of being compromised?
1. Execute `bindu-studio tls renew --node <node-id>` to force the node to generate a fresh private key pair and CSR.
2. If the physical hardware was stolen or decommissioned, remove the node from the active topology via `bindu-studio mesh remove <node-id>` and apply changes (`bindu-studio mesh apply`). Once removed from `mesh.json`, Root's mTLS listener and authhook reject all traffic from that node ID.

### Q2: What cipher suites are enforced on mTLS channels?
All TLS dialers and listeners enforce **TLS 1.2 minimum** and restrict cryptography to modern AEAD cipher suites:
- `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` / `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`
- `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` / `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`
- `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` / `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`

### Q3: How does Bindu prevent node identity spoofing?
During the mTLS handshake, Bindu's MQTT `authhook` extracts the client certificate's `CommonName` and SANs. When messages arrive on `bindu/in`, the dispatcher stamps the immutable header `$user: "mesh:<node_id>"` based strictly on the verified TLS session. Payload tampering of `$user` is ignored and normalized.

---

## 7. Operational Summary & Best Practices

| Action | Command | Typical Cadence |
|:---|:---|:---:|
| **Check Expiration** | `bindu-studio tls info` | Weekly / Automated Healthcheck |
| **Export CA for New Gateways** | `bindu-studio tls export-ca --out <path>` | During initial gateway provisioning |
| **Emergency Root Key Rotation** | `bindu-studio tls renew --self --yes` | Upon incident or pre-maintenance |
| **Emergency Node Key Rotation** | `bindu-studio tls renew --node <id>` | Upon incident or node hardware change |
| **Automatic Node Renewal** | Background daemon (`/renew-node`) | Autonomous at 80% lifetime (Day 335) |

# DOCUMENT: raw_ingress_and_mqtt_adapters_guide.md
================================================================================

# Raw Ingress & Dynamic CEL Normalization Guide: Integrating Third-Party IoT, RFID & Industrial Hardware

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Zero-Modification Edge Integration Contract**:
> You do **not** need to install a Bindu agent or node on every third-party RFID reader, PLC gateway, or BLE beacon. Commercial hardware and legacy devices publish raw, untyped MQTT streams (arbitrary JSON, plain text, or binary byte frames) directly to Bindu's raw ingress port `bindu/in/raw/#`. Google CEL reactors normalize those streams in-memory into strongly-typed Bindu semantic events with **zero SQLite WAL write amplification** and **zero mesh flooding**.

---

## 1. Architectural Motivation: Why Hardware Prefers Raw MQTT

In modern Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial IoT (IIoT) architectures, MQTT is the undisputed standard for field-level connectivity:

- **Ultra-low Footprint (Edge-Native)**: Fixed headers of just 2 bytes allow resource-constrained microcontrollers (ESP32, STM32) and legacy PLCs to publish telemetry without exhausting CPU or RAM.
- **Topological Decoupling (Pub/Sub)**: Devices connect to brokers dynamically without client-server polling loops or tight point-to-point coupling.
- **QoS & State Guarantees**: Configurable delivery semantics (QoS 0, 1, 2) and *Last Will and Testament* (LWT) provide immediate offline awareness.

However, standard commercial hardware (Impinj/Zebra RFID readers, Modbus-to-MQTT edge gateways, barcode scanners) does **not** adhere to Bindu's strict envelope schema (`$type`, `$producer`, `$when`). Forcing these devices to format messages or installing runtime software on proprietary firmware is often impossible.

Bindu solves this with the **Raw Ingress & Dynamic CEL Normalization Pipeline**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Commercial Hardware<br/>(RFID / PLC / Sensor)"] -->|"MQTT Publish<br/>bindu/in/raw/rfid/dockA"| B["Bindu Dispatcher<br/>(Ingress Boundary)"]
    B -->|"Boxes in Go RAM<br/>persist: false, routing: local"| C["RawIngressEvent<br/>(In-Memory Envelope)"]
    C -->|"Direct Actor Mailbox<br/>executioneng.Deliver"| D["CEL Reactor Set<br/>(Horn Clause Deductive Engine)"]
    D -->|"Transforms & Dedupes<br/>uint16_be, float32_be, json_parse"| E["Typed Semantic Event<br/>(e.g., TagRead, FreezerStatus)"]
    E -->|"Immutable WAL Ledger"| F[("SQLite Ledger<br/>v_messages")]
    E -->|"Mesh Forwarding"| G["mTLS Parent / Mesh"]
```

---

## 2. Ingress Boundary & Ephemeral Contract

### Raw Ingress Topics
Bindu listens for raw hardware ingress on:
- `bindu/in/raw`
- `bindu/in/raw/<subpath>` (e.g., `bindu/in/raw/rfid/dock1`, `bindu/in/raw/plc/line2`, `bindu/in/raw/sensor/temperature`)

The subpath after `bindu/in/raw/` is automatically extracted into `fields.subpath` for declarative filtering in CEL reactors.

### Envelope Packaging (`RawIngressEvent`)
The incoming packet payload is automatically inspected and boxed into an ephemeral `RawIngressEvent` without writing to disk:

| Field | Source / Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `$type` | `"RawIngressEvent"` | System message type for raw ingress events. |
| `$producer` | MQTT `client_id` (or username) | Hardware identifier of the publisher. |
| `$group` | `"ingress"` | Default group partition for raw ingress. |
| `$when` | RFC3339 UTC timestamp | Exact arrival timestamp. |
| `fields.topic` | Incoming MQTT topic | Complete incoming topic string (e.g., `bindu/in/raw/rfid/dock1`). |
| `fields.subpath` | Sub-topic path | Suffix after `bindu/in/raw/` (e.g., `rfid/dock1`). |
| `fields.content_type` | `"json"` \| `"text"` \| `"binary"` | Auto-detected payload encoding format. |
| `fields.payload` | `map[string]any` | Decoded JSON object (if `content_type == "json"`). |
| `fields.raw_data` | `string` | UTF-8 string or hex-encoded string representation. |
| `fields.raw_bytes` | `[]byte` / `string` | Raw bytes available for binary CEL manipulation. |

### The Two Guardrails: Non-Persistence & Local-Only Routing
1. **Zero SQLite WAL Bloat (`persist: false`)**: `RawIngressEvent` is marked with `persist: false`. Untyped sensor streams never hit the SQLite ledger, preventing WAL bloat from high-frequency raw telemetry.
2. **Zero Mesh Flooding (`routing: ["local"]`)**: `RawIngressEvent` cannot be routed to `"parent"` or `"child"`. Untyped traffic remains strictly within the receiving gateway node. Only normalized semantic messages are eligible for mesh forwarding.

---

## 3. CEL Binary & Parsing Extension Functions

Bindu embeds a high-performance binary parsing suite into all CEL evaluation environments (`pkg/celext`):

| CEL Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `hex_encode(bytes \| string)` | `(bytes) -> string` | Returns lower-case hex string representation of bytes. |
| `hex_decode(string)` | `(string) -> bytes` | Decodes a hex string (with or without `0x` prefix) into bytes. |
| `bytes_slice(bytes \| string, start, end)` | `(bytes, int, int) -> bytes` | Clamped sub-slice of bytes between `start` and `end` indices. |
| `uint8(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> uint` | Reads 8-bit unsigned integer at `offset`. |
| `uint16_be(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> uint` | Reads 16-bit Big-Endian unsigned integer at `offset`. |
| `uint16_le(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> uint` | Reads 16-bit Little-Endian unsigned integer at `offset`. |
| `uint32_be(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> uint` | Reads 32-bit Big-Endian unsigned integer at `offset`. |
| `uint32_le(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> uint` | Reads 32-bit Little-Endian unsigned integer at `offset`. |
| `float32_be(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> double` | Reads 32-bit IEEE 754 Big-Endian float at `offset`. |
| `float32_le(bytes \| string, offset)` | `(bytes, int) -> double` | Reads 32-bit IEEE 754 Little-Endian float at `offset`. |
| `json_parse(string \| bytes)` | `(string) -> dyn` | Dynamically deserializes JSON text/bytes into a CEL map or list. |

---

## 4. Integration Recipes

### Recipe A: Commercial RFID Reader (Untyped JSON)
Commercial readers (e.g., Zebra FX9600, Impinj R700) publish raw JSON tag reads when items cross a dock door:

**Incoming MQTT Topic:** `bindu/in/raw/rfid/dock_north`  
**Raw Payload:**
```json
{
  "tag_epc": "3034257BF400B7800004FB37",
  "read_count": 4,
  "peak_rssi": -52.4,
  "antenna_port": 1
}
```

**Target Bindu MessageType (`TagRead`):**
```json
{
  "name": "TagRead",
  "routing": ["local", "parent"],
  "retentionMode": "count",
  "retentionValue": 50,
  "properties": [
    {"name": "epc", "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "EPC identifier"},
    {"name": "antenna", "type": "integer", "required": true, "description": "Antenna port number"},
    {"name": "rssi", "type": "number", "required": true, "description": "Signal strength in dBm"}
  ]
}
```

**CEL Reactor Configuration:**
```json
{
  "reactor_id": "rfid_dock_normalizer",
  "input_message_type": "RawIngressEvent",
  "output_message_type": "TagRead",
  "trigger_condition": "payload.subpath == 'rfid/dock_north' && payload.content_type == 'json'",
  "transformation_expression": {
    "epc": "payload.payload.tag_epc",
    "antenna": "int(payload.payload.antenna_port)",
    "rssi": "double(payload.payload.peak_rssi)"
  }
}
```

---

### Recipe B: Industrial PLC / Modbus Gateway (Raw Binary Bytes)
An industrial edge computer reads an RS-485 Modbus RTU pressure/temperature transmitter and publishes a 6-byte binary payload:
- Bytes 0..3: IEEE 754 Float32 temperature (Big-Endian)
- Bytes 4..5: UInt16 status code / pressure psi (Big-Endian)

**Incoming MQTT Topic:** `bindu/in/raw/modbus/reactor4`  
**Raw Payload:** `[0x42, 0x28, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x78]` (42.0 °C, 120 psi)

**Target Bindu MessageType (`ReactorTelemetry`):**
```json
{
  "name": "ReactorTelemetry",
  "routing": ["local", "parent"],
  "retentionMode": "count",
  "retentionValue": 100,
  "properties": [
    {"name": "temperature_c", "type": "number", "required": true, "description": "Temperature in Celsius"},
    {"name": "pressure_psi", "type": "integer", "required": true, "description": "Pressure in PSI"},
    {"name": "alarm", "type": "boolean", "required": true, "description": "Over-pressure alarm flag"}
  ]
}
```

**CEL Reactor Configuration:**
```json
{
  "reactor_id": "modbus_reactor4_normalizer",
  "input_message_type": "RawIngressEvent",
  "output_message_type": "ReactorTelemetry",
  "trigger_condition": "payload.subpath == 'modbus/reactor4' && payload.content_type == 'binary'",
  "transformation_expression": {
    "temperature_c": "float32_be(payload.raw_bytes, 0)",
    "pressure_psi": "int(uint16_be(payload.raw_bytes, 4))",
    "alarm": "uint16_be(payload.raw_bytes, 4) > 100u"
  }
}
```

---

### Recipe C: Legacy Sensor or Webhook Bridge (Plain Text)
A legacy serial adapter or curl bridge sends raw plain text alerts:

**Incoming MQTT Topic:** `bindu/in/raw/gates/north`  
**Raw Payload:** `EMERGENCY_STOP_TRIGGERED`

**Target Bindu MessageType (`SafetyIncident`):**
```json
{
  "name": "SafetyIncident",
  "routing": ["local", "parent"],
  "retentionMode": "count",
  "retentionValue": 20,
  "properties": [
    {"name": "incident_code", "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Incident alert code"},
    {"name": "gate", "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Gate identifier"},
    {"name": "critical", "type": "boolean", "required": true, "description": "Critical incident flag"}
  ]
}
```

**CEL Reactor Configuration:**
```json
{
  "reactor_id": "gate_safety_normalizer",
  "input_message_type": "RawIngressEvent",
  "output_message_type": "SafetyIncident",
  "trigger_condition": "payload.subpath.startsWith('gates/') && payload.content_type == 'text'",
  "transformation_expression": {
    "incident_code": "payload.raw_data",
    "gate": "payload.subpath",
    "critical": "payload.raw_data.contains('EMERGENCY')"
  }
}
```

---

## 5. Verification & Testing

### Dry-Run Verification with `bindu-studio`
Verify your CEL normalization expressions before deploying:

```bash
# 1. Test JSON Normalization
go run ./cmd/bindu-studio cel-reactor dry-run \
  --config ./poc_cel_reactor_config.json \
  --reactor rfid_dock_normalizer \
  --payload '{
    "topic": "bindu/in/raw/rfid/dock_north",
    "subpath": "rfid/dock_north",
    "content_type": "json",
    "payload": {"tag_epc": "3034257BF400B7800004FB37", "antenna_port": 1, "peak_rssi": -52.4}
  }'

# 2. Test Binary Normalization
go run ./cmd/bindu-studio cel-reactor dry-run \
  --config ./poc_cel_reactor_config.json \
  --reactor modbus_reactor4_normalizer \
  --payload '{
    "topic": "bindu/in/raw/modbus/reactor4",
    "subpath": "modbus/reactor4",
    "content_type": "binary",
    "raw_bytes": "QiAAAAx4",
    "raw_data": "422800000078"
  }'
```

### Live MQTT Ingress Verification
Publish raw messages using standard command-line tools:

```bash
# Publish untyped JSON from standard MQTT client (e.g. mosquitto_pub)
mosquitto_pub -h localhost -p 1883 -t "bindu/in/raw/rfid/dock_north" \
  -m '{"tag_epc": "3034257BF400B7800004FB37", "antenna_port": 1, "peak_rssi": -52.4}'

# Query the SQLite WAL ledger to confirm TagRead was created and RawIngressEvent was NOT persisted
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/messages/sql \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "SELECT \"$type\", \"$producer\", fields FROM v_messages WHERE \"$type\" IN (\x27RawIngressEvent\x27, \x27TagRead\x27) ORDER BY \"$when\" DESC LIMIT 5"}'
```

**Expected Result:**
- `RawIngressEvent` count: **0** (ephemeral RAM delivery).
- `TagRead` count: **1** (persisted typed semantic fact).
