# DOCUMENT: Bindu Studio — User Guide (Command Overview).md
================================================================================

# Bindu Studio — User Guide (Command Overview)

`bindu-studio` is the operator CLI for product lifecycle, runtime rollout, mesh operations, plugins, and system configuration.

## Command Surface (Current)

Current top-level commands:

- `access-control` — access-control configuration tools.
- `cel-reactor` — inspect, export, import, merge, and validate CEL declarative transformation rules.
- `completion` — shell completion scripts.
- `config-state` — show whether config changes require restart.
- `dashboards` — export, import, list, and validate declarative dashboards.
- `doctor` — diagnostics commands.
- `fleet` — mass provision, clone, and deploy Bindu node fleets (drones, edge gateways, cloud VMs) via concurrent Go SSH (`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh`).
- `geo-locagram` — manage global WGS84 coordinates (`NodeGeoLocation`), indoor Cartesian planes (`NodeLocalGeometry`), batch import/export, offline validation, and spatial event queries.
- `hall` — hierarchical command/flag help tree.
- `help` — help for any command.
- `iso` (alias `audit`, `check`) — automated technical conformance auditing against ISO/IEC industrial standards (IEC 62443, ISO 27001, ISO 25010, ISO 42001, ISO 20922, ISO 19111).
- `license` — inspect/update installed license token.
- `lifecycle` — product import and activation.
- `mesh` — inspect/update mesh topology and node metadata.
- `message-samples` — export persisted samples from SQL and replay them through `bindu/in`.
- `message-types` — inspect, import, export, update, and hot-reload message types.
- `plugin` — create/certify/apply/remove/list plugins.
- `query` — execute read-only SQL queries and rehydrate persisted message state to target gateway nodes via `bindu/in`.
- `reset-bindu` — restart `bindu-root` using the current installation's restart mechanism.
- `rest-reactor` — inspect, export, import, merge, dry-run, and validate REST call reactor configurations.
- `root-service` — manage `bindu-root` service lifecycle.
- `runtime` — runtime desired snapshots and runtime update delivery.
- `schedule-event` — schedule, cancel, list, and purge distributed time-based events, timers, and digital twin awakening state machines.
- `secrets` (alias `integration-passwords`) — manage encrypted integration credentials, third-party API keys, and storage tokens in `accessControlConfig.brs`.
- `security` (alias `audit`, `scan`) — audit Go runtime and third-party dependencies for reachable vulnerabilities via static call-graph reachability analysis.
- `self-update` — update `bindu-studio` binary.
- `semantic-ai-reactor` — export, import, merge, dry-run, and inspect active semantic AI reactor deployments.
- `solution` — declarative MAS solution manifests and bundles (`MASSolutionSet`) for AI-driven deployment and cloning.
- `system-config` — inspect/validate system configuration.

Use this to print the live command tree from your current binary:

```bash
bindu-studio hall
bindu-studio hall --format json
```

## Intent by Domain

- Product install/update/activation:
  `lifecycle`
- Runtime config/plugins rollout to nodes:
  `runtime`
- Plugin development and assignment:
  `plugin`
- Declarative CEL, REST, and Semantic AI Reactors:
  `cel-reactor`, `rest-reactor`, `semantic-ai-reactor`
  *(Note: All reactor validation commands strictly enforce the Anti-Recursion Safety Invariant `E_REACTOR_RECURSIVE_LOOP` — output/response message types cannot match trigger/input message types).*
- Distributed Time-Based State Machine & Timers:
  `schedule-event` (`schedule`, `cancel`, `list`, `purge`)
- Geospatial & Indoor Cartesian Planes:
  `geo-locagram` (`list`, `show`, `set`, `delete`, `geocode`, `local-plane`, `local-set`, `local-delete`, `import`, `export`, `validate`, `query`)
- Observability and Visualizations:
  `dashboards`
- Query & Node State Rehydration:
  `query` (`bindu-studio query rehydrate`), `message-samples`
- Mesh topology, live diagnostics, node control, and emergency recovery:
  `mesh` (topology: `tree`, `add`, `bulk-add`, `edit`, `move`, `delete`, `remove`, `apply`; diagnostics: `health`, `ping`, `node-presence`, `node-status`, `node-version`; control: `node-refresh`, `node-restart`; recovery: `rescue-parent`, `rescue-all`)
- Configuration and policy:
  `system-config`, `access-control`, `license`
- Operational tooling & security:
  `doctor`, `security`, `iso`, `config-state`, `root-service`, `reset-bindu`, `self-update`

## Guide Map

- Plugins: `bindu-studio-plugin-user-guide.md`
- CEL Reactors: `cel_reactor_user_guide.md`
- REST Reactors: `rest-reactor-user-manual.md`
- Semantic AI Reactors: `AISemanticReactorSet Schema & Authoring Guide for AI.md`
- Scheduled Events & Time Engine: `scheduled_events_user_guide.md`
- Geo-Locagram & Spatial Semantics: `bindu-studio-geo-locagram-user-guide.md`
- Dashboards: `dashboards_user_guide.md`
- SQL Queries & State Rehydration: `queries_user_guide.md`
- Mesh: `Bindu Studio Mesh User Manual.md`
- Node deploy/runtime rollout details: `Bindu Studio Mesh Node Deployment.md`
- Lifecycle (product import/activation): `lifecycle-user-manual.md`
- System config: `Bindu Studio - System Configuration User Guide.md`
- Access control: `Bindu Access Control User Manual.md`
- MAS Solutions & AI Cloner: `bindu_studio_solution_user_guide.md`

## Notes

- Hidden/internal commands are not part of operator workflows and are intentionally excluded from this guide.
- The authoritative source is always the running binary (`bindu-studio hall` / `bindu-studio <cmd> -h`).

## Scheduled Events & Timers Highlights

Notable `schedule-event` workflows for edge time orchestration:

```bash
# 1. Schedule a 30s delay timer on edge node
bindu-studio schedule-event schedule \
  --node node-dell-1 \
  --id silo-quarantine-batch-001 \
  --action recondition_wakeup \
  --producer lot-potato-4891 \
  --group coldchain \
  --delay-sec 30 \
  --payload '{"batch_id":"BATCH-4891","target_fryer_temp":178.5}'

# 2. Inspect active timers and awakening history
bindu-studio schedule-event list --node node-dell-1

# 3. Cancel a pending timer
bindu-studio schedule-event cancel --node node-dell-1 --id silo-quarantine-batch-001 --reason "Manual batch release"

# 4. Purge completed and expired timers from the ledger (leaves active future schedules)
bindu-studio schedule-event purge --older-than 24h
```

## Query & Rehydration Highlights

Notable `query` workflows for programmatic state rehydration:

```bash
# Rehydrate latest world geometry to a specific gateway node
bindu-studio query rehydrate \
  --sql 'SELECT * FROM v_messages WHERE "$type" = '\''NodeLocalGeometry'\'' ORDER BY "$when" DESC LIMIT 1' \
  --targets node-1 \
  --auth console:Pass123

# Rehydrate MAS solution set to multiple edge nodes with JSON output
bindu-studio query rehydrate \
  --sql 'SELECT * FROM v_messages WHERE "$type" = '\''MASSolutionSet'\''' \
  --targets node-1,dell-debian1 \
  --auth console:Pass123 \
  --json
```

## Runtime Highlights

Notable `runtime` workflows in the current CLI:

- `bindu-studio runtime baseline status|diff|accept`
- `bindu-studio runtime desired show|commit`
- `bindu-studio runtime update wizard`
- `bindu-studio runtime config-backup list`
- `bindu-studio runtime config-backup create --note "..."`
- `bindu-studio runtime config-restore <backup-id>`

`runtime config-backup` and `runtime config-restore` are local root operations over `runtime/config`; they do not require `--auth`.

## Mesh Operations & Recovery Highlights

Notable `mesh` workflows for operational diagnostics and disaster recovery:

```bash
# 1. Cluster-wide health snapshot
bindu-studio mesh health

# 2. Inspect node presence, advertised IP endpoints, and lane readiness
bindu-studio mesh node-presence dell-debian1
bindu-studio mesh presence node-1 --json

# 3. Pull deep runtime telemetry (CPU, RAM, disk, active BPR plugins, reactors)
bindu-studio mesh node-status dell-debian1

# 4. Measure end-to-end mTLS MQTT ping round-trip time
bindu-studio mesh ping node-1 --count 3 --auth console:StrongPass123

# 5. Trigger immediate state telemetry recalculation from an edge node
bindu-studio mesh node-refresh dell-debian1 --reason "Post-rollout audit" --auth console:StrongPass123

# 6. Graceful edge node service restart
bindu-studio mesh node-restart node-1 --reason "Applying kernel updates" --yes --auth console:StrongPass123

# 7. Targeted emergency ParentPresence rescue (after node IP drift)
bindu-studio mesh rescue-parent --node-id dell-debian1 --node-ip 10.0.5.52 --auth console:StrongPass123

# 8. Batch emergency ParentPresence rescue across multiple nodes (subnets drift)
bindu-studio mesh rescue-all --nodes "node-1=10.0.5.51,dell-debian1=10.0.5.52" --yes --auth console:StrongPass123
bindu-studio mesh rescue-all --inventory /etc/bindu/production-nodes.txt --yes --auth console:StrongPass123
```

## Security & Vulnerability Auditing Highlights

`bindu-studio security audit` performs static call-graph reachability analysis against the official Go Vulnerability Database (`govulncheck`), ensuring zero false positives by alerting strictly on vulnerabilities actively reachable in compiled code paths:

```bash
# 1. Standard reachable vulnerability audit
bindu-studio security audit

# 2. Audit with verbose breakdown (including uncalled transitive dependencies)
bindu-studio security audit --show-all

# 3. Machine-readable JSON output for automated CI/CD and DevOps ingestion
bindu-studio security audit --format json
```

## ISO/IEC Industrial Conformance Auditing

`bindu-studio iso audit` executes an automated conformance test harness across the Bindu Core Engine, generating empirical audit dossiers mapped to official ISO/IEC standards:

```bash
# 1. Full automated ISO/IEC compliance audit
bindu-studio iso audit

# 2. Audit specific industrial standard
bindu-studio iso audit --standard iec-62443
bindu-studio iso audit --standard iso-25010
bindu-studio iso audit --standard iso-42001

# 3. Export official JSON audit evidence dossier for CISO/auditor review
bindu-studio iso audit --format json --out ./dist/bindu-iso-report.json

# 4. Generate living Markdown conformance dossier
bindu-studio iso audit --format markdown --out ./docs/LIVE_ISO_AUDIT_REPORT.md
```

## Fleet Provisioning & Mass Drone Deployment (Concurrent Go SSH)

`bindu-studio fleet deploy` orchestrates mass provisioning, template-based topology cloning, and parallel rollouts across fleets of drones, edge gateways, and cloud VMs using native Go SSH (`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh`):

```bash
# 1. Mass deploy 50 drones using IP range and auto-naming by IP
bindu-studio fleet deploy \
  --template "drone-template" \
  --ips "10.0.1.1-10.0.1.50" \
  --ssh-user "pi" \
  --ssh-password "raspberry" \
  --naming "bn-{ip}" \
  --concurrency 25

# 2. Deploy using a JSON inventory with dynamic MAC address discovery
bindu-studio fleet deploy \
  --template "drone-template" \
  --inventory ./drones-fleet.json \
  --naming "drone-{mac}" \
  --concurrency 30

# 3. Simulate and preview node ID resolution without modifying the mesh or executing installations
bindu-studio fleet deploy \
  --template "drone-template" \
  --ips "192.168.10.0/28" \
  --naming "drone-{index:03d}" \
  --dry-run --json
```




================================================================================
# DOCUMENT: AI Agent Fleet Deployment and Bulk Add Tutorial.md
================================================================================

# AI Agent Fleet Deployment & Bulk Add Tutorial

This guide is designed for AI Coding Agents and DevOps automation scripts to understand, execute, and program against the headless fleet deployment and bulk node addition subcommands in **Bindu Studio**.

---

## 1. Node Addition in Bulk: `mesh bulk-add`

Before generating deployment packages, the nodes must exist in the mesh topology. Instead of interactive prompts, use `mesh bulk-add` to register nodes programmatically.

### Command Syntax

```bash
bindu-studio mesh bulk-add \
  --pattern "<id-pattern>" \
  --platform "<os>/<arch>" \
  --parent "<parent-node-id>" \
  --connectivity "<gateway|reference>" \
  [--mesh "<path-to-mesh.json>"] \
  [--base "<base-dir>"]
```

### Pattern Expansion Rules for AI Agents

*   **Numeric Ranges**: Use curly braces with double dots, e.g. `{1..100}`.
    *   **Zero-Padding**: If the start or end boundary has leading zeros (e.g., `{01..10}`), the command automatically formats all expanded IDs with the same width (e.g., `01`, `02`, ..., `10`).
*   **Alphabetic Ranges**: Use lowercase range `{a..z}` or uppercase `{A..Z}` (e.g., `{a..e}`).
*   **No Range**: If no range is specified (e.g., `node-pi-5`), it behaves as a single add operation.

### Step-by-Step Registration Example

1.  **Bulk Add Nodes**:
    ```bash
    bindu-studio mesh bulk-add --pattern "node-pi-{01..12}" --platform "linux/arm64" --parent "root" --connectivity "gateway"
    ```
2.  **Commit Draft Changes**:
    The bulk-add subcommand validates the draft schema and writes changes to `mesh.draft.json`. To apply these changes to the active mesh, run:
    ```bash
    bindu-studio mesh apply
    ```

---

## 2. Packaging the Fleet: `mesh node-deploy`

Once the nodes are registered, package the node software and configuration in a generic form.

### Command Syntax

```bash
bindu-studio mesh node-deploy \
  --generic \
  --platform "<os>/<arch>" \
  [--out "<output-directory>"]
```

### Outputs Produced

1.  **`bindu-node-generic-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz`**:
    *   Contains launcher, installer, and root configuration files.
    *   **Crucial for Automation**: It does **not** contain any node identity files (the `identity/` directory is omitted).
2.  **`fleet-deploy.json`**:
    A manifest file detailing the bootstrap configurations, CA certs, and enrollment token:

```json
{
  "bootstrap": {
    "parent_id": "root",
    "mqtt_candidates": ["192.168.1.10:1888"],
    "signing_url": "https://192.168.1.10:8448/api/v1/tls/sign-node",
    "root_ca_pem": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n..."
  },
  "enrollment": {
    "token": "active-enrolment-token-xyz"
  },
  "nodes": [
    {"node_id": "node-pi-01", "target_ip": ""},
    {"node_id": "node-pi-02", "target_ip": ""}
  ]
}
```

---

## 3. Native Fleet Deployment Orchestration: `bindu-studio fleet deploy`

Instead of writing fragile custom Python or Bash scripts with external `scp` and `ssh` subprocess loops, Bindu provides a native, highly concurrent Go orchestrator built into the CLI: **`bindu-studio fleet deploy`**.

### Architecture & Key Capabilities

1. **Zero-Disk Streaming (CGO-Free Go SSH)**:
   Connects using `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` and pipes the compressed generic payload directly to the remote machine's `tar -xzf -` over the SSH session's stdin. No temporary `.tar.gz` files on remote disks, no multiple SCP round-trips.
2. **Semantic Template Cloning**:
   Clones an existing, fully configured node (`--template <node_id>`) with its assigned MAS plugins (`bindu-cv`, `hello-world`), MQTT channels, ports, and CEL reactors across all target units.
3. **Dynamic Hardware Discovery & Naming**:
   Supports patterns such as:
   - `bn-{ip}`: e.g. `bn-10-0-1-42`
   - `drone-{mac}`: inspects remote network interface (`/sys/class/net/*/address`) and formats hardware MAC.
   - `drone-{index:03d}`: zero-padded numeric indices (`drone-001`, `drone-002`).
   - `node-{machine-id}`: unique Linux system machine-id (`/etc/machine-id`).
4. **Concurrent Worker Pool**:
   Deploys to hundreds of machines in parallel with configurable goroutine pools (e.g. `--concurrency 30`), achieving $<3$ minutes rollout across 400 drones.

### Command Examples

```bash
# 1. Deploy 50 drones via IP range with automatic naming by IP
bindu-studio fleet deploy \
  --template "drone-template" \
  --ips "10.0.1.1-10.0.1.50" \
  --ssh-user "pi" \
  --ssh-password "raspberry" \
  --naming "bn-{ip}" \
  --concurrency 25

# 2. Deploy using a JSON inventory with dynamic MAC address discovery
bindu-studio fleet deploy \
  --template "drone-template" \
  --inventory ./drones-fleet.json \
  --naming "drone-{mac}" \
  --concurrency 30

# 3. Simulate and preview node ID resolution without modifying the mesh or executing installations
bindu-studio fleet deploy \
  --template "drone-template" \
  --ips "192.168.10.0/28" \
  --naming "drone-{index:03d}" \
  --dry-run --json
```

---

## 4. Legacy / External Script Orchestration (Python / Shell Reference)

If integrating with external CI/CD or legacy orchestrators, you can still consume `fleet-deploy.json` directly:

### Pseudocode for Custom External Scripts

```python
import json
import subprocess

# 1. Load the fleet manifest
with open("dist/nodes/fleet-deploy.json") as f:
    manifest = json.load(f)

token = manifest["enrollment"]["token"]
generic_bundle = "dist/nodes/bindu-node-generic-linux-arm64.tar.gz"

# 2. Iterate and deploy
for node in manifest["nodes"]:
    node_id = node["node_id"]
    
    # Resolve target IP (if blank in manifest, lookup from agent's inventory)
    target_ip = node["target_ip"] or my_inventory.lookup_ip(node_id)
    
    # Copy the generic bundle to the target machine
    subprocess.run(["scp", generic_bundle, f"bindu@{target_ip}:/tmp/bindu-node.tar.gz"], check=True)
    
    # Extract and execute the installer using enrollment token overrides
    install_command = (
        f"tar -xzf /tmp/bindu-node.tar.gz -C /opt/bindu && "
        f"/opt/bindu/bindu-install-node "
        f"--node-id {node_id} "
        f"--enrollment-token {token} "
        f"--yes"
    )
    subprocess.run(["ssh", f"bindu@{target_ip}", install_command], check=True)
    
    print(f"Node {node_id} successfully enrolled and started!")
```

### Command Run on Node Target:

#### Option A: Authenticating with Enrollment Token (Recommended for head-less / mass deploy)
```bash
./bindu-install-node --node-id <node_id> --enrollment-token <token> --yes
```
*   **`--node-id`**: Forces the node identity.
*   **`--enrollment-token`**: Authenticates the preflight request with the Root using the header `X-Enrollment-Token`, bypassing interactive Basic Auth prompts.
*   **`--yes`**: Auto-confirms all installer options (non-interactive mode).

#### Option B: Authenticating with Root Admin Credentials (Alternative/Dev)
If no active enrollment tokens are configured in the Root Coordinator's `binduConfig.json` (located at `runtime/config/binduConfig.json`), the deployment CLI will fallback to using the default token `"one-time-token-valid-for-24h-abc"`. 
To enroll using this fallback token, the operator must manually add the token to the Root Coordinator's `binduConfig.json` inside the `"enrollment_tokens"` array and restart the coordinator service (`sudo systemctl restart bindu-root`).

Alternatively, to avoid modifying config files, the operator can pass the Root Coordinator's console credentials directly:
```bash
./bindu-install-node --node-id <node_id> --root-user console --root-pass <your_console_password> --yes
```
*   **`--root-user`**: Root Coordinator console administrator username.
*   **`--root-pass`**: Root Coordinator console administrator password.
*   **`--yes`**: Auto-confirms all installer options (non-interactive mode).

Once completed, `bindu-node` is launched under systemd. It will automatically announce its presence and ports back to the Root Coordinator.

# 🤖 AGENTS.md — AI Solution Creator Adapter for Bindu MAS

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **CANONICAL SPECIFICATION NOTICE**:
> This file is a lightweight entrypoint adapter for **OpenAI Codex, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Agentic Toolchains**.
> 
> The authoritative, model-agnostic architectural specification governing how AI Agents design, validate, package, certify, and deploy Multi-Agent System (MAS) solutions on Bindu is located in:
> 
> 👉 **[`public/console/docs/BINDU.md`](./BINDU.md)**

## Mandatory Instruction for Autonomous Agents

When tasked with creating, modifying, deploying, or verifying a Bindu MAS solution, business schemas (`poc_message_types.json`), CEL kinetics, AI semantic reactors, dashboards, BPR plugins, or tutorials:

1. **Read Canonical Specification:** Consult [`public/console/docs/BINDU.md`](./BINDU.md) for the complete 3-Layer Invariants, Level 0 DAG, the 6 Standard Artifacts, and the Universal 5-Phase Deployment Pipeline.
2. **Zero-Plaintext Wire Guarantee:** Never emit plaintext credentials in JSON manifests or wire payloads. Always use `"secret:KEY_NAME"` or `secret('KEY_NAME')` backed by the encrypted vault (`accessControlConfig.brs`).
3. **Validation-First Discipline:** Always execute `bindu-studio <cel-reactor|semantic-ai-reactor|rest-reactor|plugin> dry-run` with representative payloads before deployment. Syntactic `validate` alone is never sufficient.
4. **Native Observability:** Query ledger state strictly via the native REST endpoint `POST /api/v1/messages/sql` on `v_messages`. Never inspect raw `.db` files directly on disk.
5. **Deductive Logic vs. Perceptual AI (Horn Clause Contract):** CEL reactors execute formal Horn clause deduction ($P_1 \land P_2 \dots \rightarrow Q$) in sub-microsecond Go memory. AI models (SLMs, VLMs, TypeSafe `Jev`) are strictly **Ground Term Extractors** ($P_1$) or bounded synthesizers. Never delegate business policy, safety cutoffs, or threshold derivations to an unconstrained AI prompt.
6. **Mobile & Leaf Client Rule:** When developing mobile applications (Android/iOS) or handheld terminal integrations, NEVER embed or run a `bindu-node` daemon inside mobile OSes. Implement mobile devices strictly as Leaf Clients over MQTT TLS/mTLS following [`mobile_and_leaf_client_guide.md`](./mobile_and_leaf_client_guide.md) and reference wrappers in [`mobile-client-sdk/`](./mobile-client-sdk/).

Refer to [`BINDU.md`](./BINDU.md) for full architectural patterns, CLI cheat sheets, and the 15 MAS archetypes.
